title: The Treasure Under the Mango Tree

pages.text: On Saturday, Grandpa Dzah gave Yayra a hand-drawn map. ‘Start at the well,’ he said. ‘Ten steps north, then five steps east. There is a surprise waiting.’ ‘A treasure!’ cried Yayra.
sentences: On Saturday, Grandpa Dzah gave Yayra a hand-drawn map.
‘Start at the well,’ he said.
‘Ten steps north, then five steps east.
There is a surprise waiting.’ ‘A treasure!’ cried Yayra.
pages.alt: An old man hands a girl a hand-drawn map beside a well.

pages.text: Yayra and her cousin Kojovi stood at the well. ‘Which way is north?’ asked Kojovi. Yayra pointed to the compass on her school bag. ‘The sun rises in the east,’ she said, ‘so north is on our left.’
sentences: Yayra and her cousin Kojovi stood at the well.
‘Which way is north?’ asked Kojovi.
Yayra pointed to the compass on her school bag.
‘The sun rises in the east,’ she said, ‘so north is on our left.’
pages.alt: Two children stand at a well, one pointing at a small compass.

pages.text: They walked ten steps north. They stopped. Then five steps east. They stopped again. Nothing. Only dust and a few ants. ‘The map must be wrong,’ sighed Kojovi.
sentences: They walked ten steps north.
They stopped.

They stopped again.
Nothing.

pages.alt: The children stand in an empty patch of ground looking disappointed.

pages.text: Yayra thought. ‘Wait. Grandpa’s legs are very long. Maybe his steps are longer than ours.’ They measured one of Grandpa’s steps with the metre stick. It was about 80 cm. Then they measured their own steps. About 50 cm.
sentences: Yayra thought.

pages.alt: The children measure steps with a metre stick on the ground, with Grandpa watching.

pages.text: ‘Grandpa’s ten steps are 10 × 80 cm, which is 800 cm, or 8 metres,’ said Kojovi. ‘One of our steps is 50 cm, so we need 800 ÷ 50 = 16 steps.’ ‘And his five steps east are 400 cm,’ said Yayra, ‘so we need 8 of ours.’
sentences: ‘Grandpa’s ten steps are 10 × 80 cm, which is 800 cm, or 8 metres,’ said Kojovi.
‘One of our steps is 50 cm, so we need 800 ÷ 50 = 16 steps.’ ‘And his five steps east are 400 cm,’ said Yayra, ‘so we need 8 of ours.’
pages.alt: The children write sums on the ground with a stick.

pages.text: They went back to the well and walked sixteen small steps north. Then eight small steps east. Right in front of them stood the old mango tree, with a swing hanging from its branch.
sentences: They went back to the well and walked sixteen small steps north.
Then eight small steps east.

pages.alt: The children count steps along a path to a large mango tree with a swing.

pages.text: Grandpa Dzah knelt by the roots. He gently moved the loose soil with a trowel, and lifted out a small tin box. Inside were three marbles, a faded photograph and a letter written long ago.

pages.alt: An old man shows the children a small tin box with marbles and a photograph.

pages.text: ‘I buried this when I was a boy,’ said Grandpa. ‘These are my marbles. The letter is to the child who finds it.’ Yayra read it aloud: ‘Be curious, be kind, and always measure twice.’ The end.
